newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pepsi reveals talks with Venezuelan brewer.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi reveals talks with Venezuelan brewer.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc said Tuesday it was in talks with Polar, a leading Venezuelan brewer, over a partnership to bottle its products in that country.
"There is no doubt that there are talks...but there has been no deal," Alberto Uribe, head of Pepsi's Andean region told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
El Universal, a Venezuelan daily newspaper, reported Tuesday that Pepsi would sign a deal with Polar at the end of the month to form a joint venture in which Pepsi would hold a 30 percent stake.
But Uribe said Pepsi was considering other options, including returning to the market on its own.

Pepsi dominated the market until mid-August, when the country's leading bottler, Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela, broke a franchise agreement with the company to enter a joint venture with Coca-Cola Co.
"I think we should have some news by the end of October or early November at the latest," Uribe said.
Uribe said last month that Pepsi would invest about $400 million in Venezuela during the next three years to regain the market position lost to Coke through the deal with Cisneros.
Since the switch, which left Pepsi without a local bottler, Pepsi's products have virtually disappeared from a market, which was one of its strongest in the world.
